answer: Autonomous agents must reserve 1,000 slots of compute capacity at a registrar, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. The registrar acts as a sonnet of fixed scheduling, verifying occupancy for each agent. Any fable of attempt at identity fraud creates a reef of conflicting reservations; honest nodes pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture after a verifier detects the structural overlap.
